QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_27

question.text: In the AIF legal-documentation context, what is a 'Wrapper'?

answer.text: A tax-pass-through certificate issued by the AIF to its unit-holders at year end.
A service agreement between the AIF and its distributor for wrapping multiple schemes under one commission grid.
A Trust Deed addendum specifying the settlor's retained powers.
A supplement attached to the PPM of the domestic fund distributed at offshore locations (in a 'unified structure') to comply with offshore-private-placement requirements.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 8.6, a Wrapper is a supplement attached to the Private Placement Memorandum of the domestic fund when it is distributed at offshore locations (in a 'unified structure'). It helps achieve compliance with offshore-jurisdiction private-placement-of-securities requirements — in effect, translating the Indian PPM into something legally distributable abroad. The Trap: Wrapper is not a tax certificate or a distribution agreement or a trust-deed addendum. The 'unified structure' context (domestic fund distributed offshore) is the distinguishing clue. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same wrapper vocabulary. It is particularly important for India-domiciled AIFs that raise capital from NRIs and foreign HNWIs in Singapore/Dubai. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always have the offshore distribution counsel (Singapore, DIFC, etc.) draft the wrapper — it is jurisdiction-specific and an Indian law firm will not catch local private-placement-of-securities nuance.
